messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: Dedicated pool 'nebula-ded-pool' - node gpu-node-18 reporting repeated ECC errors and heartbeat flaps. Impact: 1/6 GPUs degraded, tenant 'nebulahealth' experiencing increased latency and OOM errors. Auto-escalation to on-call.

matt_oncall: Ack. I'm on it. @ash_infra can you pull the node logs and confirm hardware vs driver? If hardware, we should prepare a drain/replace and isolate tenant workloads.

ash_infra: Pulling logs now. Seeing repeated NVML ECC single-bit and then multi-bit counts incrementing on GPU0 and GPU1. Also dmesg shows PCIe AER errors. Likely hardware-level. Copying relevant lines:

ash_infra: ```
[ 12345.678901] NVRM: GPU 0000:65:00.0: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 13, pid=4128, GPU has fallen off the bus.
[ 12345.679002] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 79, GPU has a persistent ECC error.
[ 12345.679103] pcieport 0000:00:1c.0: AER: Corrected error received: id=0000
```

matt_oncall: Ok, thanks. @lee_runtime any immediate mitigation at the serving layer? Can we evict sessions pinned to that GPU and fail traffic to fallback variants?

lee_runtime: We can trigger a node drain which will gracefully move active sessions off that node, but some large KV cache entries may be lost — that will cause a small cold-start latency spike for affected tenants. We have a fallback routing policy for enterprise: route to same-model hosted variant for up to 20% of requests or fallback to dedpool spare nodes. For NebulaHealth we already have a 'burst-to-hosted' policy enabled. We should throttle burst so cost doesn't explode.

jess_support: I'm messaging NebulaHealth (account contact: @cora_nebula) to let them know we're investigating. Any ETA for mitigation?

ash_infra: If we do an immediate cordon+drain, replacement time depends on available spare nodes in the dedicated cluster. Could be 12-25 minutes to reprovision a replacement instance and reattach NVMe. If hardware swap needed, longer. I recommend draining and failing over to the spare pool + burst-to-hosted as fallback.

olivia_acct: I'll notify AE and Legal (since Nebula is in VPC with strict ingress rules). We need to confirm whether bursting to hosted API is permitted under their contract/secure routing. @sam_cx can you confirm any restrictions?

sam_cx: Nebula flagged that data-in-transit must stay inside the VPC unless approved. They allowed 'encrypted egress to hosted endpoints' only as a temporary mitigation if we route via a private peering link. I already spun up a temporary peering tunnel last quarter. We can use it but must log all requests. I'll standby with the onboarding key.

matt_oncall: Good. Action plan:
1) cordon gpu-node-18 to prevent new pods/sessions
2) drain existing sessions gracefully, with immediate eviction for <1min stuck sessions
3) route NebulaHealth traffic per policy: spares -> burst-to-hosted via peering, cap at 15% initial
4) open support ticket with on-site hardware team and schedule RMA if ECC persists

matt_oncall: I'll run the drain now. Command:

matt_oncall: ```
# cordon + drain (internal orchestration)
redwoodctl node cordon gpu-node-18 --reason "ECC errors"
redwoodctl node drain gpu-node-18 --timeout 90s --evict-force
``` 

ash_infra: running now. Starting eviction hooks. Will watch for stuck sessions. Also pausing autoscaler for that podgroup to avoid new nodes landing on unhealthy host.

ash_infra: ```
redwoodctl autoscaler suspend --pool nebula-ded-pool
``` 

lee_runtime: Routing change in flight: shifting 15% of routing to hosted via peering. Watch for rate limit spikes and spike in token cost. enabling extra batching to absorb cold cache penalty.

jess_support: Update from Nebula: "We see 503s for some requests, but overall system is running. Thanks for the heads up." They asked for an ETA. I've told them ~20-30m initial mitigation.

ash_infra: Drain progress: 12 sessions remaining, 2 sessions stuck >60s trying to flush KV cache. Forcibly evicting.

ash_infra: ```
redwoodctl session evict --node gpu-node-18 --force --session-age>60s
``` 

matt_oncall: After eviction, monitor NebulaHealth SLAs and logs for error surge >1.5x baseline. @lee_runtime keep an eye on quality regressions when routing to hosted (some model versions differ slightly).

lee_runtime: Will run targeted evals on sample prompts from NebulaHealth (prompt set 'nebula-regress-1') and watch for P0s. Setting up a smoke evaluation every 2 minutes.

sam_cx: Nebula agrees to bursting via peering for up to 45 minutes. They request logs of every routed request — I'll enable verbose audit logging for the peering tunnel.

ash_infra: Node drained. Marking gpu-node-18 as 'isolated' and starting reprovision of replacement. Spare allocation attempt #1 failed (insufficient quota in region-us-west2). Starting attempt #2 in region-us-east1.

ash_infra: reprovision started. ETA ~22 minutes. Opening hardware ticket for physical replacement if repro fails.

matt_oncall: Good. Current impact: NebulaHealth 95th latency +220ms, error rate up from 0.4% -> 1.6% during eviction window. No other tenants affected. Logging this as customer-impacting incident. Moving to P1.

olivia_acct: AE notified, legal on standby. I'll prepare the post-incident comms template for Nebula.

lee_runtime: Smoke evals show minor quality diffs for hosted model (tokenization leading to <1% score drop). No immediate rollback needed but note in RCA.

ash_infra: Replacement node provisioned and joining cluster. Running node health checks and NVMe attach. If checks pass, we'll uncordon and let scheduler rebalance.

ash_infra: Health checks green. Uncordoning.

ash_infra: ```
redwoodctl node uncordon gpu-node-245-replacement
``` 

ash_infra: Rebalance started. Neat: sessions rehydrate from prefix cache slowly. Latency back to baseline in 6 minutes.

jess_support: Nebula: "Thanks, we're seeing traffic normalize. Please send postmortem and logs." They requested confirmation that no customer data left cluster during burst.

sam_cx: All peering-routed requests were encrypted and proxied through the private tunnel. Audit logs are enabled; will hand over to Nebula security once postmortem is ready.

matt_oncall: Incident status: mitigated. Replacement node healthy, no more ECC errors on new host. Marking incident as resolved, continuing to monitor for 2 hours. Assigning post-incident actions:
- infra: run hardware diagnostics + RMA for gpu-node-18 (ash_infra)
- runtime: add stronger fallback test to canary (lee_runtime)
- devex/support: update runbook for tenant peering bursts (jess_support)
- account: confirm contract/burst permissions in writing (olivia_acct)

matt_oncall: Handoff to next on-call @kara for night shift. Kara, I'll leave logs and timeline in the incident task. All critical mitigations complete. If you need anything, ping me.

next_oncall_kara: Taking handoff. Thanks @matt_oncall. I'll watch SLAs and vendor RMA status. Marking on-call owner in channel. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: Incident P1 closed by matt_oncall at ts 1880005900. Postmortem task created: /tasks/INC-1880004321-rca

matt_oncall: Adding one note for RCA: consider increasing spare node quota in us-west2 for Nebula-dedicated pools to avoid cross-region reprovision latency. Also add forced KV flush timeout to 45s to avoid long stalls during drains.

jess_support: I'll draft the customer-facing summary and attach logs. Will defer to legal for wording re: data egress during peering.

sam_cx: Confirmed Nebula security is okay with the peering audit approach. They want the RCA within 48 hours.

matt_oncall: Closing thread. Thanks everyone."
